novum_candidates.description: The story is a first-person domestic narrative about William Durrant, a materialistic and self-deluded husband whose marriage fails because of his own emotional blindness. It contains no science-fictional, technological, or otherwise world-altering element.

novelty.rationale: There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm. The setting is early twentieth-century Philadelphia and New York, involving business, marriage, cards, and infidelity\u2014entirely consistent with the authorial empirical reality. No new object, technology, social order, or condition estranges the world.

cognitive_validation.rationale: With no novum present, there is no imaginary science or systematic new logic to validate. Cognitive validation is inapplicable to a purely realist domestic story.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The narrative is governed by ordinary character psychology and a mundane marital breakdown, not by any novum. No estranging element determines the story's logic.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: No reader-facing cognitive estrangement is created; the story presents a recognizably ordinary social world without any novum to defamiliarize it.
